rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes cold spray deposition, whereas the paper used spark plasma sintering to make electrodes and then electrospark deposition to apply coatings. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions low-temperature processing (below 200°C) and aggressive service environments (salt spray, chloride). The paper used high-temperature SPS (850–1050°C) and ESD under argon, with no corrosion testing performed. The conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes low-temperature impact consolidation, compressive residual stresses, and fine-grained structure to improve hardness and corrosion resistance. The paper's mechanism involves high-temperature diffusion during SPS and pulsed spark melting/rapid solidification during ESD, leading to phase changes, porosity reduction, and superficial defects. These are different mechanism classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance versus fusion welding and untreated surfaces. The paper predicted improved densification and integrity with higher SPS temperature and more defects with additional ESD layers, and did not measure wear or corrosion. The predicted properties and comparisons differ.
